truth_evidence: Affected every release before 3.1.4; fixed in 3.1.4 (the 3.1.3 fix only rejected whitespace; '/', '>' and '=' in keys still inject attributes).
Fix commit 0668239, the merge of the GHSA-h75v-3vvj-5mfj advisory PR, in tag 3.1.4 and not in 3.1.3. https://github.com/pallets/jinja/commit/0668239dc6b44ef38e7a6c9f91f312fd4ca581cb
Module level in src/jinja2/filters.py: _space_re = re.compile(r"\s") is replaced by _attr_key_re = re.compile(r"[\s/>=]"); the regex is the check that was too weak.
do_xmlattr: uses _attr_key_re and a new error message; the rest of the change is docstring.

do_xmlattr is a template filter. Nothing in Jinja calls it by name: filters.FILTERS holds it, Environment.__init__ copies that table into self.filters (DEFAULT_FILTERS.copy()), and it runs either from compiled template code (compiler.py pull_dependencies writes t_N = environment.filters['xmlattr'] into the generated module and the filter use site calls it) or from Environment.call_filter('xmlattr', ...), which looks the name up in self.filters and calls it.

Entry points: the names that render a template (Template.render, render_async, generate, generate_async, stream, make_module, make_module_async), Environment.call_filter, and the classes whose instances carry the filter table (Environment, Template, the sandbox subclasses). Unlike the attr advisory, the injection needs no sandbox, so plain Environment and Template are listed.

A call-graph walker cannot derive these entry points, since the only reference to do_xmlattr in the source is the FILTERS dict literal; they are expected from data/overrides.json. The scan side can see that a project renders templates; it cannot see whether a template uses |xmlattr, so a match on these entry points means 'reachable, template content not checked', not a confirmed use of the filter.
